title: BPM Ft. The BloodFunks

segments.text: Back porch meditation,

Taking in the rays of the rising sun, deep breathing tendency, tree pollen in my lungs, doing yoga while you sleeping in, I'd say I've already won. I consider this liquid straight to my tongue. I kept looking for beginnings, then look back where I'd be willing. I started writing with a purpose instead of rapping for fun, embarrassed about my old work, but I'm proud of what I became. Just like any chapter, there's always another page. Flip the sheet of paper, read along to the change. Stop measuring success on how much money you make. Stay focused on your mental health and physical state. I still can't believe I eased away from heat of spoons and needles. Now I just smoke a little weed and eat an asshole.
Music then release it to these random people for them to see that they too can defeat their evils. Yeah. I'm no longer in the demon's reach, filled in the blanks, feels like I finally found peace.
Hold on now. Stop the beat.

Sometimes I say nothing at all. I just share my thoughts with God while I stare at the wall. My phone's ringing, but I'm ducking the call. Play my songs if you wanna hear me talking to y'all. Skateboarding taught me there's no way that I'm not gonna fall, so I've been spending my free time with a medicine ball.
Wall sits in
bare cross. Step on the scale though, I swear that it's broken or flawed.
Slimming down, but it still say two eighty. Whatever. I'm being sexy and I know it, so it doesn't faze me. Positive energy.
Yeah. I radiate it. I stay consistent with my early morning back porch meditation.
Yeah.
That's what put me in the best mood.

Bananas in the blender with some fresh fruit. I'm trying to make a smoothie the other day, but I put too much in there. I bought the Sky this afternoon and found a crescent moon. When I was younger, I wanted to be a moony tongue or auto rocket, but my Walmart wheels wouldn't move. I had holes all in my basketball shoes. My mom was mad I was kick flipping my I threes.
Pop showed me Houdini Biz and EZ E.

The Manhattan's and the Bee Gees. I swore DJ Premier and Guru made the hardest team. Little did he know, in those moments, pop sparked dreams. Yeah. Now I'm the one that's blaring through his speakers.
Doc Ellis somehow, someway, throwing heaters. I got a band behind me now. Let's book a theater. I found your old music and I didn't like it. Yeah. Me neither.

I used to drunk and freestyle on any beat play. Drunk at the zoo, worst project that I ever made. Extremely high after dying really felt strange. Don't trip is when my reality had rearranged. Music city miracle
created a wave. Hardest my pain and wet. Weighs on my heart and brain. If I'm a thousand with myself, there's no takeaways.
My past had highs, but I always battled hesitation.
Every obstacle in a complicated situation.

How I act about commitment show that I'm evasive. Mistakes were drawn with Sharpie. I can't erase it, learn from my past actions, then fully embrace them. Take it in. I used to spend all day sedated, sat in my room alone and laughed at my imagination.
I painted through hallucinations.
Now I'm high. I'm consistently morning back porch meditation.
Yeah.

It's safe to say I broke the mold, but I hate to say that all it took was that overdose. I used to sit at home, drink pep, shovel Coke in my nose. Now when I'm alone, I smoke balls and refold all my clothes. All these Gen Z rappers really think they're cold. Auto tune on, originality is gone. A bunch of Fortnite dance songs and sing alongs. I forgot I'm a part of the last generation that grew up without phones we had.

A dinosaur computer sitting in the kitchen. I was picking a mice based image. Yo, if practice makes perfect, I'm a never ending scrimmage. Guess I really am my own competition. Let's have a toast to commitment. I'm here to gather commission. I stay lathered with ambition. They hate to admit I'm rapping now. Me going in as a given, I fell away from my vision. But for the first time, I get to say I'm back now. Yeah.... Minute, man. Let me ask you something. Don't hit me with no stupid questions. What the hell? I'll answer passive aggressive thought it was obvious from past projects. I was headed a bad direction, had to unmask myself and triple check the reflection. Your
favorite rapper's a lack of a message. Soon enough, his dumbass will have a tad of his necklace.
Have a sad dramatic exit, but that alone should teach a lesson.

I think the game's out of control with no one left to ref it. Only d one has big enough balls to ever address it. All these stupid ass kids that were never neglected on drugs, buying guns as props instead of protection.
They call that flex.
That's why I practice patience.
Early
morning, back porch meditation.
